paragraphs.title: The Locust Army and the Day of the Lord

easy.explanation: Joel says, “for the day of the LORD cometh, for it is nigh at hand.”
easy.q: What does Joel say is near?

answers: A day of darkness and gloominess
easy.explanation: The passage calls it “a day of darkness and of gloominess.”
easy.q: How is the coming day described?

easy.explanation: The army is described as “a great people and a strong.”

answers: Like the garden of Eden before it and a desolate wilderness behind it
A wilderness before it and a forest behind it
medium.explanation: Joel contrasts the fruitful land before the army with the desolation left behind it.
medium.q: What is the land like before and behind the army?

medium.explanation: The word describes the people’s great fear and distress.
medium.q: What does the word “pained” mean in “the people shall be much pained”?

answers: They march every one on his ways and do not break their ranks
medium.explanation: The army marches in order and does not break its ranks.
medium.q: Which detail shows that the army is organized?

challenge.explanation: The army runs with the appearance and speed of horses and horsemen.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to horses and horsemen emphasize?

answers: The people are distressed, the earth quakes, and the heavens tremble
The people rejoice, the land blossoms, and the heavens brighten
The people sleep, the land is peaceful, and the stars shine
challenge.explanation: The passage describes distress, an earthquake, trembling heavens, and darkened lights.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the world’s response to the army?

answers: It is great and terrible, and no one can endure it
It is distant and without effect
challenge.explanation: The passage asks, “who can abide it?” after calling the day great and very terrible.
challenge.q: What does the ending emphasize about the day of the LORD?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Repentance and a Fasting Assembly

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “turn ye even to me with all your heart.”
easy.q: To whom are the people told to turn?

easy.explanation: The passage calls for fasting, weeping, and mourning.
easy.q: What actions are associated with their turning?

answers: The whole congregation, including elders and infants
easy.explanation: The people, elders, children, and those nursing are all summoned.
easy.q: Who is gathered for the solemn assembly?

answers: Repentance must be inward, not merely outward
medium.explanation: The people are told to rend their hearts rather than merely performing an outward sign.
medium.q: What is the contrast between rending the heart and rending garments?

answers: A journey away from the city
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a formal and serious gathering of the people.
medium.q: What does “solemn assembly” mean in this passage?

answers: To ask the LORD to spare His people
To invite the people to a feast
medium.explanation: They plead, “Spare thy people, O LORD.”
medium.q: Why do the priests weep between the porch and the altar?

answers: The call to repentance includes the entire community
challenge.explanation: Even the bridegroom and bride are called from their private rooms to join the assembly.
challenge.q: What does the inclusion of the bridegroom and bride show?

answers: He is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness
challenge.explanation: These qualities are given as reasons for turning back to Him.
challenge.q: Which description of the LORD encourages the people to return?

answers: That the heathen will ask, “Where is their God?”
That the harvest will be too large
That the bride and groom will not arrive
challenge.explanation: They ask that God’s heritage not be given to reproach among the heathen.
challenge.q: What concern do the priests express in their prayer?

paragraphs.title: The Lord Shows Compassion and Restores Blessing

easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD will “pity his people.”
easy.q: On whom does the LORD have pity?

easy.explanation: The LORD promises corn, wine, and oil.
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to send?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will remove far off from you the northern army.”
easy.q: What will the LORD do to the northern army?

answers: Both lead to restoration and protection
medium.explanation: The LORD responds by showing compassion, restoring food, and removing the army.
medium.q: What is the connection between the LORD’s care for His land and His pity for His people?

medium.explanation: A barren land is dry, empty, and unable to produce crops.
medium.q: What does “barren” mean in the description of the land?

answers: Toward the east sea and the utmost sea
Toward the city and the houses
medium.explanation: The army is driven toward the east sea and the utmost sea.
medium.q: Toward which places is the northern army driven?

answers: The army will be destroyed and become a source of foul odor
The army will continue ruling the land
The army will become a harvest
challenge.explanation: Its stink and ill savour rise because it has been destroyed after doing great things.
challenge.q: What does the army’s final stench suggest?

answers: Reproach is replaced by satisfaction and restoration
Day is contrasted with night only
A bride is contrasted with a groom
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises food and says He will no longer make His people a reproach among the heathen.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in this passage?

answers: The people will receive abundant and sufficient food
The people will receive only a little food
The people will leave the land
challenge.explanation: The promise describes restored provision sufficient to satisfy the people.
challenge.q: What is implied by the promise, “ye shall be satisfied therewith”?

paragraphs.title: The Joy of the Land and the Renewal of the Crops

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “Fear not, O land.”
easy.q: To whom is the command “Fear not” addressed?

answers: The pastures, trees, fig tree, and vine
easy.explanation: The pastures will spring, and the trees, fig tree, and vine will produce.
The passage says, “the floors shall be full of wheat.”

answers: Because the LORD is restoring the land and its crops
medium.explanation: The LORD’s blessing brings renewed pasture, fruit, rain, and harvest.
medium.q: Why are the land, the beasts, and the children of Zion called to rejoice?

answers: Rain that comes later in the growing season
Grain that has already been harvested
medium.explanation: The latter rain is the later seasonal rain that helps bring the crops to maturity.

answers: The floors are full and the fats overflow with wine and oil
medium.explanation: The rain leads to abundant wheat, wine, and oil.
medium.q: What results from the rains mentioned in the passage?

answers: From fear and desolation to joy and fruitfulness
challenge.explanation: The land and its inhabitants move from fear into renewed prosperity and rejoicing.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in this passage?

answers: The restoration affects the whole environment
The beasts are enemies of the people
The beasts are leaving the land
challenge.explanation: The beasts are told not to fear because the pastures are being renewed.
challenge.q: What does the mention of the beasts of the field suggest?

answers: The sound of a trumpet alone
challenge.explanation: Full floors and overflowing wine and oil provide concrete evidence of abundance.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the blessing is tangible and abundant?

paragraphs.title: Compensation, Abundance, and Knowledge of the Lord

answers: The years eaten by the locusts
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten.”
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to restore?

answers: Praise the name of the LORD
easy.explanation: They will eat, be satisfied, and praise the name of the LORD.
easy.q: What will the people do after eating in plenty?

answers: That He is in the midst of Israel and there is none else
That He is far from Israel
That He has no connection with the land
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I am in the midst of Israel... and none else.”
easy.q: What will the people know about the LORD?

answers: Restoration results in abundant food and contentment
Restoration is only a memory of the past
medium.explanation: The restored years are expressed through eating in plenty and being satisfied.
medium.q: How are restoration and satisfaction connected?

medium.explanation: The LORD calls the locusts His great army, which He had sent among the people.
medium.q: What does “my great army” refer to in this passage?

answers: Eating and satisfaction, praise, and knowledge of the LORD’s presence
medium.explanation: The passage connects restored food with praise and recognition that the LORD is among Israel.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the result of the blessing?

answers: The removal of reproach and lasting security
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the restored people will no longer bear shame.
challenge.q: What does the repeated promise that God’s people will never be ashamed emphasize?

answers: It leads the people to praise and recognize the LORD
It causes the people to forget the LORD
It prevents the people from gathering
challenge.explanation: The people’s satisfaction is followed by praise and knowledge of God’s presence.
challenge.q: How does abundance lead beyond physical satisfaction?

answers: The LORD restores what was lost and renews His relationship with His people
The locusts continue to rule a ruined land
The people must leave their land
challenge.explanation: The passage combines restoration, abundance, praise, and the assurance that the LORD is in the midst of Israel.
challenge.q: Which idea best summarizes these verses?
